title: The Classic of Filial Piety
attributionNote: The treatise is traditionally ascribed to Zengzi recording the words of Confucius, but is generally dated to the Warring States or early Han. Its eighteen short chapters set out the duty of filial piety from the son of heaven down to the common people.
description: The Classic of Filial Piety is the short text that made filial duty the root of Confucian ethics: filial piety in the son of heaven, the princes, the ministers, the officers and the common people, the three powers, government by the sages, the five punishments, remonstrance, and mourning for parents. It was read in every school and used by rulers to argue that the state is a family writ large.
historicalContext: The classic was commented on by emperors and became one of the most widely printed books in China; its place in the examination canon was secured with the rest of the Confucian corpus. Legge translated it, with the Chinese text, for the Sacred Books of the East, volume 3 (1879).
availabilityNote: Complete: the eighteen printed chapters in Legge's translation, streamed from the Internet Sacred Text Archive at read time, one chapter per page. The translator's introduction and his note on the translation are volume apparatus and are not part of the work.
